finding: Metadata overhead slightly reduces theoretical quantization savings.
evidence: With group size 128, int8 effective reduction is about 74.22% and int4 effective reduction is about 86.72%.
why_it_matters: Realistic quantization estimation must include scale/zero-point storage.

finding: Metadata overhead affects int4 more than int8 proportionally.
evidence: Average metadata overhead is about 3.12% of raw int8 parameter memory and 6.25% of raw int4 parameter memory.
why_it_matters: Lower-bit formats have smaller raw weight memory, so metadata becomes relatively more important.

finding: Larger group sizes reduce metadata overhead.
evidence: Group size 256 stores fewer scale/zero-point groups than group size 32.
why_it_matters: There is a tradeoff between quantization granularity and metadata memory.

finding: This simulation is still analytical, not real runtime quantized execution.
evidence: The simulation adds metadata assumptions but does not load or run int8/int4 kernels.
why_it_matters: It prevents overclaiming measured runtime savings.

finding: Quantization mainly reduces parameter memory, not necessarily all runtime memory.
evidence: Activations, KV cache, temporary buffers, and allocator behavior may remain unchanged.
why_it_matters: A full memory estimator must separate parameter memory from total GPU memory.
